changes_from_v1: v1's cohort (pilot-cohort-proposal.md v1) had 19/200 non-Latin-script hotels (11 Thai, 8 Japanese), several confirmed non-hotels -- fixed by adding gate 12 (Latin-script name, docs/seo-policy.md §2). Also: 4 real hotels whose own source address contradicted their extraction city (a Bora Bora resort + a Fiji resort in 'Sydney', a Bali villa in 'London', a Bali hotel with a self-contradicting address in 'Singapore') were found via a systematic destination-name search and excluded from the dataset entirely -- docs/reports/destination-name-mismatch-audit.md. This pack was regenerated against the resulting v2 200-hotel proposal: London and New York picks changed (their v1 picks weren't in v2's top selection); the other 10 cities' picks are unchanged and still valid against v2 data (Rome, Tokyo, Bangkok, Dubai, Singapore, Barcelona, Sydney, Paris, Lisbon, Amsterdam weren't affected by either fix).
selection_method: 12 of the 200 v2 pilot-cohort hotels, one per launch city, chosen to cover: varied cities (all 12 represented), both independent and chain-flagged entities, both high and gate-borderline confidence, and 2 cases judged the most discutable in the full list -- see each hotel's selection_reason. Not a random or statistically representative sample; a deliberately varied inspection set, same spirit as Phase 2's 18-hotel inspection.

hotels.selection_reason: Most discutable pick #1 (unchanged from v1). The name ("Boys' Home") strongly suggests a juvenile residential-care institution, not a bookable hotel -- despite formally passing every automated gate (confidence 81.8, dedupe 100, matched Overture's lodging taxonomy, and a Latin-script name so gate 12 doesn't catch it either). This is exactly the failure mode entity_qa.py's English-market name-pattern filter is built to catch, and "home" isn't currently one of its exclusion markers -- adding it isn't done here, only flagged, since a blind marker addition risks new false exclusions elsewhere. If this is genuinely a hotel with an unfortunate name, publishing it is harmless; if it's a mislabeled institution, publishing it would be a real, reputationally serious category error. Recommend the owner verify this one specifically before it goes live, independent of its gate status.
